title: Speedometer wiki
intro: Every gauge, light, style and setting on your dashboard: what it shows, and how to set it up.
metaTitle: Speedometer Live Wallpaper wiki: every gauge, light and setting
metaDescription: Every gauge, warning light, style and setting of Speedometer Live Wallpaper for Android: what each one shows, and how to set it up.
source: Written from the app's screens and strings, version 2.0.4 with 19 styles (Games main bb6ac7d4, 26 Oct 2026), after the 2.0.0 text of 17 Oct (Games main 39aa208).

art.alt: Three phones on a car's dashboard at night showing the Classic, Amber Night and Future designs, with rain and city lights on the windscreen

sections.title: The big gauge
sections.intro: The dial in the middle. It shows one of three things; pick it in the style's settings (Customize), tap it on your home screen, or use the Big gauge tile.

sections.title: Small gauges
sections.intro: The four dials around it, and the little temperature dial.

sections.title: Warning lights
sections.intro: Lights on the big gauge and the small gauges. Each warning light can be switched off in Customize → Warning lamps.

sections.title: Clock, settings & help
sections.intro: The digital clock, every setting, and answers to common questions.

sections.title: Styles
sections.intro: 19 styles. Classic, Steel and Graphite are free; every other style is a one-time purchase, or unlock them all at once. Pick one on the Styles screen.

entries.name: The big gauge
entries.summary: One dial, three jobs: power, CPU clock or GPS speed.
what: The big gauge shows one of three things: power, CPU clock or GPS speed. The digits above the needle show the same value as the needle.
how: Pick the mode in Customize → Big gauge, tap the gauge on your home screen, or use the Big gauge tile in Quick Settings to switch. Each style keeps its own mode.

entries.name: Big gauge tile
entries.summary: A Quick Settings tile that switches the big gauge on any phone.
what: Some launchers, Samsung's included, don't pass taps on to the wallpaper, so tapping the big gauge does nothing there. The Big gauge tile in Quick Settings switches the mode on every phone, in the same order: power, CPU clock, GPS speed.
Its subtitle shows the mode the gauge is in now. It skips modes your phone can't show, like CPU clock on phones that don't allow reading it.
how: On Android 13 and later, Settings → Big gauge tile → Add puts it in your Quick Settings for you.
Or open the Quick Settings editor and drag Big gauge into your tiles.

entries.name: Power mode
entries.summary: Watts going into or out of the battery.
what: In power mode the needle shows the watts going into the battery (to the right, while charging) or out of it (to the left, with a minus).
how: Plug in your charger and watch the needle swing right: a quick way to see how fast a charger really is.
facts: Tap the gauge or the Big gauge tile

steps.text: Pick Power in Customize → Big gauge, tap the gauge on your home screen, or use the Big gauge tile.
Plug in your charger and watch the needle swing right: a quick way to see how fast a charger really is.
On battery the needle swings left, with a minus.

gauge.label: Power gauge
gauge.offText: On battery: the needle swings left, with a minus.

entries.name: CPU clock mode
entries.summary: How fast the processor runs, as a share of its top speed.
what: In CPU clock mode the needle shows how fast the processor runs right now, as a percentage of its top speed.
how: Some phones don't allow apps to read the CPU clock. On those, the gauge shows -- instead of a number; use power or GPS speed instead.

entries.name: GPS speed mode
entries.summary: Your speed in km/h or mph, with a red mark at your top speed.
what: In GPS speed mode the needle shows your speed. A red mark shows the top speed of the current drive.
GPS speed needs your precise location while the wallpaper is on screen. It is used only to read your speed and never leaves the phone.
how: Choose GPS speed in Customize → Big gauge; the app explains why it needs location, then Android asks. Pick "Precise" when it does.
Switch between km/h and mph in Customize → Units. Settings → Speed unit is the unit every style follows until you change its own.
If location is off for the app, the gauge can't read your speed: allow precise location in the app's settings.

entries.name: Signal
entries.summary: Top left: your mobile signal, from 0 to 4 bars.
what: The small gauge at the top left shows your mobile signal, from 0 to 4 bars.

entries.name: RAM
entries.summary: Top right: how much of the phone's memory is in use.
what: The small gauge at the top right shows how much of the phone's memory is in use.

entries.name: Wi-Fi
entries.summary: Bottom left: Wi-Fi strength, status and link speed.
what: The Wi-Fi gauge shows the strength of your Wi-Fi signal.
Under it, a status line reads CONNECTED, NO NETWORK, MOBILE DATA or DISABLED. When connected, it also shows the link speed in Mbps.

entries.name: Battery
entries.summary: Bottom right: how full your battery is.
what: The battery gauge shows how full your battery is. Its LOW light comes on at the low battery level, and the green bolt lights while the phone charges.

entries.name: Battery temperature
entries.summary: The little dial: from cold (C) to hot (H).
what: The small dial inside the battery gauge shows the battery's temperature, from the low temperature (C) to the high one (H).
how: Set what counts as low and high in Customize → Warning lamps; the warning lights use the same limits.

entries.name: Low battery light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: the battery is at or below your low level.
what: Lights when the battery is at or below the low battery level: 15 % unless you change it.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Low battery switches the light off, and Low battery level changes the limit.

entries.name: Bluetooth light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: Bluetooth is on.
what: Lights while Bluetooth is on.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Bluetooth switches it off.

entries.name: High temperature light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: the battery is hotter than your limit.
what: Lights when the battery is hotter than the high temperature: 45 °C unless you change it.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → High temperature level sets the limit.

entries.name: Low temperature light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: the battery is colder than your limit.
what: Lights when the battery is colder than the low temperature: 0 °C unless you change it.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Low temperature level sets the limit.

entries.name: Charging bolt
entries.summary: On the battery gauge: the phone is charging.
what: The green bolt on the battery gauge lights while the phone charges.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Charging switches it off.

entries.name: LOW light
entries.summary: On the battery gauge: the battery is low.
what: The LOW light on the battery gauge comes on at the low battery level.

entries.name: Wi-Fi ON light
entries.summary: On the Wi-Fi gauge: green on Wi-Fi, yellow on mobile data.
what: The ON light on the Wi-Fi gauge is green while you're on Wi-Fi and yellow on mobile data.

entries.name: Date and time
entries.summary: The LCD under the big gauge.
what: The LCD under the big gauge shows the date and the time.
how: In Customize → Clock you can set the time format (12 h, 24 h or the phone's), whether seconds show, the date order, and the time and date separators.

entries.name: Settings
entries.summary: The app's settings, and each style's own in Customize.
what: Tap the gear at the top of the home screen for the app's settings. Each style's own settings are in Customize, on the home screen and on the Styles screen.
how: Wallpaper: the style in use, Motion and battery (Saver, Balanced or Smooth) and the Big gauge tile.

New styles start with: the speed unit and the clock every style follows until you change its own, and Copy settings to all styles, which gives every style one style's big gauge, units, clock, lamps and needle motion. Each style keeps its own layout and look.
Permissions: GPS speed (location) and Music, calls and messages (notification access).
Previews and feedback: live previews and vibration.
Purchases: Unlock all styles and Restore purchases.
Privacy: Ad choices (where your region requires it) and the privacy policy. About: the Guide, Rate on Google Play and the licences.

Customize, for one style: the big gauge's mode and top-speed mark, units, clock, warning lamps, music, calls and messages, and the look (colours, glow, background, needle feel and the start-up sweep). Changes show at once in the preview, and Reset puts the style's defaults back.

entries.name: Setting it as your wallpaper
entries.summary: Set as wallpaper, confirm, done; and how to get it back.
what: Open the app and tap Set as wallpaper, then confirm on the preview. The button turns amber and reads On your home screen: the dashboard is now your wallpaper.
how: If you force-stop the app or clear its data, Android puts your old wallpaper back. Open the app and tap Set as wallpaper again.
The wallpaper never shows ads.
notes: Speedometer Live Wallpaper is for Android phones and tablets only: iPhones don't allow live wallpapers from other apps.

entries.name: The Styles screen
entries.summary: All 19 styles, drawn live: use one, buy one, or pick its layout.
what: Open the app and tap Styles. Your styles come first, then the rest, each drawn live by the wallpaper itself with its name and its state: In use, Free, Owned or Locked. Tap one for its page: a live demo you can pause, Power, CPU and Speed buttons, its description and its layouts.
how: Tap Use this style to switch: the wallpaper changes at once.
Tap Buy to buy a style through Google Play, or Unlock all for every style and layout, including the styles still to come. Google Play shows the price for your country.
Under Layouts, pick a layout and tap Use this layout. Edit layout moves and resizes the gauges of a layout you can edit, and Make your own saves your arrangement as the style's own layout.
notes: If a payment is still pending, or Google Play isn't available, the screen tells you.

entries.name: Classic style
entries.summary: Free: the 2016 dashboard with five gauges, four lights and an LCD clock.
what: Classic is the original 2016 dashboard on a brushed-metal background: the big gauge with signal and RAM behind its shoulders, Wi-Fi and battery below, four warning lights and the LCD clock.
It's free, like Steel and Graphite, and it's the style you start with. It never asks for notification access.

entries.name: Future style
entries.summary: The 2016 chrome cluster, rebuilt, as a one-time purchase.
what: Future is one big chrome dial that follows the same three modes as Classic (power, CPU clock or GPS speed), with the value in its blue glass hub and battery and RAM arcs at the bottom.
Above it, the clock and date. Below it, the music area, the Bluetooth and Wi-Fi status, and how many calls you missed and messages you haven't read.
In landscape, on tablets and unfolded foldables, it becomes the 2016 two-dial cluster: the big gauge on the left, mobile signal and battery temperature on the right, music in the middle.
how: Buy it once on the Styles screen, or get it with Unlock all. It's a one-time purchase, not a subscription.
Tap the dial, or use the Big gauge tile, to switch its mode.
The music and the call and message counts need notification access.

entries.name: Music, calls and messages
entries.summary: On Future: the song that's playing, missed calls and new messages.
what: Future shows the song that's playing, with its cover and the media volume, and how many calls you missed and messages you haven't read.

For that, Android has to give the app notification access. Android warns that an app with it could read all your notifications: this one only reads the song that's playing and counts missed calls and messages. Nothing leaves your phone.
how: The app asks after you pick or buy Future. You can also turn it on in Customize → Music, calls and messages → Notification access, or in Settings → Permissions.
Without access, the music area reads MUSIC AND CALLS ARE OFF: the volume bar still works and the counts are hidden.
You can turn the access off any time in Android's settings.
notes: Calls and messages are counted from their notifications, never from your call log or your messages. Classic never asks for notification access.

entries.name: Restoring your styles on a new phone
entries.summary: Bought once, back by themselves on any phone with the same Google account.
what: Every style you buy, and Unlock all, is a one-time purchase tied to your Google account. The app checks your purchases with Google Play every time you open it, so on a new phone signed in with the same account, they come back by themselves.
how: Install the app on the new phone, open it once, then pick your style on the Styles screen. If one is missing, tap Settings → Restore purchases.
Your purchases are also remembered on the phone, so the wallpaper never waits for Google Play.
notes: A refunded purchase is removed the next time the app checks.
